title: Impact Backlog Playlist — Daphne Ruiz
content:
Context: working personal backlog for the quarter. Mix of OKR drafts, rapid experiments, and weekly check-ins. This is intentionally messy — scratchpad for commitments, confidence scores, and small bets.

-- Short elevator: goal is to increase DX (developer experience) adoption signals while freeing 20% more focus time for deep work by Q1 end.

Draft Objective A (v0.3): Make it frictionless for teams to try Redwood in a day.
- KR A1: Move trial->first-successful-call conversion from 12% -> 30% (baseline: 12% as of 2024-08).
- KR A2: Reduce average time-to-first-successful-call from 3.2 hours -> <= 45 minutes (measure: onboarding funnel timestamps).
- KR A3: Publish 4 reference apps + one quickstart video (baseline: 1 reference app).
- Confidence: 40% (need PM buy-in on funnel tracking and a small infra hook).

Draft Objective B: Reduce dev friction for internal teams and cut unplanned interrupts.
- KR B1: Decrease average interrupt time (pages + DMs flagged urgent) from 2.1 hours -> 1 hour via runbooks/automation.
- KR B2: Ship two automation playbooks to mute common noise (rollbacks, canary flaps) and test with one squad.
- KR B3: Move 50% of recurring docs into templated quickstarts (baseline: ~10% templated).
- Confidence: 60% (we own docs + a little SRE help).

Weekly check-in snippets (sprint 2025-01-13 -> 2025-01-19):
- Monday: hacked together a minimal quickstart template (md + postman collection). Slacked to #devexp for smoke test. Got 3 quick replies; two said "works on first try". -> small win.
- Tuesday: paired with Marcus 1hr; instrumented funnel events in staging (RDW-1234). Discovered event duplication edge-case — flagged to infra. TODO: add dedupe in lambda.
- Wednesday: Recording for quickstart vid postponed; need a clean demo environment. Q: do we spend 2d on infra or do low-fi camera + narration? Lean: low-fi to hit KR count.
- Friday: retro mini: too much context switching; knocked out only 60% of personal plan. Action: block 3x 2hr deep-work chunks next week.

Retrospective (Micro): What went well: quick experiment got immediate feedback; people value "first success" more than docs length. What didn't: infra telemetry gaps, and too many small asks ate deep work.

Open hypotheses to test (experiment backlog):
- H1: A 3-minute screen-recorded quickstart increases conversion vs a 10-step written doc. (A/B test on funnel page)
- H2: A one-click starter repo (preconfig) drops time-to-first-call by >50%.
- H3: Templates + prefilled example keys reduce support threads by 30%.
Plan: run H1 first (low engineering), measure for two weeks, then H2 if signal strong.

Personal metrics tracker (how I'll measure weekly):
- Deep work hours (target 12/week) — capture in calendar blocks.
- Quickstart created (count) — target 1/week for first 4 weeks.
- Funnel events instrumented (yes/no) — binary milestone.
- Interrupts handled in <1h (percentage) — track via Slack threads and incident tags.

Decisions/To-dos (rough):
- ACTION: draft quickstart video script + 20% storyboard — due 2025-01-24. (blocking: clean demo env)
- ACTION: add dedupe to staging event pipeline — RDW-1234 assigned to Marcus (due 2025-01-20).
- ACTION: create one-click repo seed (low-fi) with ENV notes — prototype by 2025-02-02.
- QUESTION: push for PM metric ownership to include trial funnel? If not, we will maintain private dashboard.

Notes to self / scratch:
- Keep notes short in the quickstart: "first call in <5 steps". People remember small wins.
- Consider recording terminal + voiceover rather than full-screen slides.
- Remove jargon: avoid internal feature names in public quickstart.
- If infra work becomes blocking >2d, pivot to narrated demo + repo.

Archive/links for quick access:
- funnel event spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/DEVEXP/Funnel-Events (draft)
- prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devexp-quickstarts (branch: daphne/one-click)
- tracker issue: RDW-1234

Closing note: This doc is living. I will snapshot a cleaned version into Confluence (DEVEXP personal playbook) once KRs are stable and we have 2 reproducible quickstarts. For now, use as single-pane-of-glass for experiments and weekly commitments.

-- end of scratchpad (leave messy; it's useful).
